# Observer retention and passivity ledger

The output hard ceilings are 200,000 JSON value/key tokens and 16 MiB serialized UTF-8 bytes. The former is a conservative semantic-entry measure: it counts every object/array/string/number/bool/null value and every object key. Thus every nested span coordinate, child, argument, field, slot and type entry is counted even when serialized on one JSONL line. Counter carries quote/escape/primitive-token state across formatter writes. Counters run before try_reserve_exact and the second, storing formatting pass. Each origin formatter validates its original file and UTF-8 range before writing.

Requested auxiliary retention is independent of the output String and compiler source/AST/index/HIR/type owners. The whole-file request buffer is fallibly reserved at 256 KiB+1 and read through Take; its allocation moves without copying into the descriptor String. At most 1,024 requests are processed sequentially, each ID<=128 bytes and source/output paths<=4,096 bytes. Fixed-field parsing and duplicate scans borrow descriptor slices and allocate no side collection. DESCRIPTOR_OVERLAP accounts 256KiB+1 + two 4096-byte paths +128 label bytes +16 String headers (a conservative allowance for path/name/format headers). This bound is admitted before candidate processing. Output filename construction happens after observe returns and fits this allowance while the final output String remains live.

Trace retention is admitted through out.aux before the allocator pre-reserves its exact declared row count. At most 200,000 ReserveEvent rows are retained; checked row-width multiplication precedes allocation. In bounded mode record only writes admitted slots, setting a failure flag and discarding later events on overflow; the complete observation then fails. Reservation request/attempt/failure/try_reserve/result behavior is unchanged. The trace row width is measured in each summary. The loader adds four fixed usize counters to this cfg(test) allocator only, for actual lex/parse attempts/completions; counter overflow likewise fails observation. No WorkMeter event or semantic observation log is enabled. Its existing current-phase field is read through a cfg(test) getter; no vector is added.

Display-map duplication is admitted before copying: path bytes + source UTF-8 bytes + (newline_count+1)*sizeof(usize) + sizeof(SourceFile) per file. Strings use try_reserve_exact; SourceMap::try_add uses its normal fallible row/line reservation. Its allocator has a zero-retention observer trace, intentionally ignored because display rendering is not candidate reservation evidence. This bounds every display copy and row before allocation. All copied paths are fixture-relative and source IDs/text are unchanged. Source-row text is directly formatted into the output buffer, with no additional owned string.

Diagnostic admission explicitly limits each actual diagnostic to <=2 secondaries and <=2 notes before rendering. This matches owned_diagnostic::MAX_LABELS=2/MAX_NOTES=2; loader diagnostics are independently required to satisfy that same observer shape ceiling or receive incomplete-observation, without changing the compiler result. This adapter does not promise a complete rendering for arbitrary larger third-party Diagnostic objects.

Before either production renderer runs, let T be the sum of UTF-8 lengths of code, stage, message, ordered secondary messages, ordered notes and every display-map path. The checked conservative temporary allowance is B=16384+128*T. There are at most three spans, all numeric fields bounded by usize decimal width; 16384 covers all punctuation/numerals, temporary String/Vec headers and up to two secondary/note vectors and their joins. JSON escaping expands one source byte by at most six and human escaping by at most ten. Across primary/secondary span strings, escaped text temporaries, joins, returned human string, returned JSON string and its appended newline, the same path can occur at most three times per representation and text inputs occur in at most a small fixed number of intermediates. 128*T conservatively covers these simultaneously retained requested payloads, including the human string while JSON renders. The output String is accounted separately; quoting the retained human/JSON into that output is checked by the two-pass output writer. No renderer reads full source-line snippets.

B must fit both remaining serialized-output budget and MAX_BYTES minus retained auxiliary bytes before either renderer allocates. The footer reports auxiliary_requested_bytes (retained descriptor/trace/display allowance), auxiliary_peak_requested_bytes (maximum retained+B over diagnostics), diagnostic_render_bound_bytes (maximum B), and descriptor_overlap_bound_bytes. These are checked requested-payload bounds, not capacities, allocator RSS or a universal process-OOM promise. Transient diagnostics are dropped after each row, so their sum across diagnostics is not retained.

Resolution facts are copied directly into the one output String before typeck consumes the resolved owner. No secondary HIR/type/source inventory vector exists. The adapter verifies functions.len()==signatures.len()==index.function_count and records.len()==index.record_count before its zip; summary binds all three actual vector totals. Every inner vector emits its full length plus complete rows/entries. Typed views assert vector completeness in the unchanged owner API; the external comparator separately checks the emitted rows cover those full vectors. Fixed Output counters, token-counting state, helper formatters and four loader counters are stack/header overhead; measured Rust owner layouts belong to the independent compiler resource ledger.

Observer work is passive and separate: two formatting traversals of each emitted value; one AST validation/inventory scan, one per-module syntax-selection inventory scan, one resolved vector walk, one complete typed vector walk, one reservation trace walk, and bounded O(request_count^2) duplicate checking (<=1024 requests) of bounded descriptor slices. Only the single normal SourceOwner whole-project selector plus resolve/type consumes the compiler WorkMeter. This is not a claim that all legacy compiler work is metered.
